title: DeepGOF-1: pretrained goodness-of-fit test for logistic regression — weights, training corpus, benchmark harness and per-replicate results
description:
The complete research compendium for DeepGOF-1: A Pretrained Convolutional Goodness-of-Fit Test for Logistic Regression with a Computable Consistency Certificate.

DeepGOF-1 is a goodness-of-fit test for logistic regression whose statistic is a convolutional network trained once, offline, on simulated departures and shipped frozen (18,273 parameters). The network reads the fitted model's residual map — a 6×6 grid of standardized residual sums over the ranks of the two strongest covariates — and the p-value is the rank of the observed score inside the analyst's own parametric bootstrap, so the level is a property of the calibration rather than of what the network learned.

This deposit contains everything needed to reproduce the paper and to train a successor:

  • R/ and inst/extdata/ — the deployable test in pure base R with the frozen weights and a cross-language verification bench (base R reproduces the training framework to 5e-11).
  • training/ — the exact training corpus (8,400 labelled residual maps), the corpus generator (the one file a successor edits), the training script and the exporter, with the row-major/column-major porting trap documented.
  • benchmark/ — the thirteen-arm evaluation harness: the reproduced Liu et al. (2024) settings, a nine-scenario severity lattice, a sixty-cell design grid, and the consistency-certificate scripts.
  • results/ — every per-replicate p-value behind every table and figure in the paper.
  • speckit/ — the frozen pre-declarations for every gate, so a successor version is judged against the same criteria, including the criteria this version failed.

The deployable test alone is also distributed as deepgof1() in the R package ebrahim.gof (version 2.6.0 and later). Code is MIT-licensed; deposited results, corpora and weights are CC-BY-4.0.

notes: The training corpus and the deposited per-replicate results are large by design: they exist so that a referee can check any number in the paper without rerunning multi-CPU-day simulations, and so that a successor version (DeepGOF-2) can be trained by editing a single file and evaluated against the same frozen criteria.
